author: Sbush27
quote: Rockstar seems to have forgotten what made Grand Theft Auto great in the first place. The franchise built its reputation on outrageous satire, dark humor, unapologetic characters, and making fun of absolutely everyone. Now there’s growing concern that GTA 6 is going to lean too heavily into modern social messaging, forced inclusivity, and watered-down cultural commentary instead of delivering the edgy, irreverent experience fans have loved for decades.I don’t play GTA to be lectured about modern social issues, political correctness, or whatever cultural trend is dominating the news cycle. I play it to escape reality, cause absolute mayhem, experience an entertaining story, and laugh at a world where nothing is off limits.There’s a difference between clever satire and checking contemporary cultural boxes. There’s also a difference between having diverse characters and making their identities or social messaging the centerpiece of a **** has always been provocative. That’s the point. It should be equally willing to offend everyone, mock every side, and refuse to play by modern cultural expectations.Hopefully Rockstar remembers that GTA is supposed to be Grand Theft Auto, not a domesticated, corporate-approved version of the franchise.**Bring back the edge. Bring back the chaos. Stop trying to make GTA politically comfortable.**
